intended_object: Any function f : α → β on a finite measurable space with measurable singletons, viewed as a simple function (finite range, measurable fibers). Inferred from the docstring and the name.
explanation: The definition keeps f as the underlying function. Each fiber f⁻¹'{x} is a finite set, so it is measurable because singletons are measurable. The range is finite because α is finite. Both hypotheses are needed. Without `Finite α` the range can be infinite. Without `MeasurableSingletonClass α` the fibers need not be measurable: with the trivial σ-algebra on a two-point type, the identity map is not measurable. Replacing finiteness with countability would not be enough either, since the range could then be infinite. The definition is a natural constructor at the right generality. It is not a special case of a more general Mathlib construction.
